answer: One robust defense ties influence to sunk hardware cost rather than raw identity count. Each agent identity must be bound to a unique trusted-execution chip with remote attestation, like a ferrous anchor that can only be minted once per physical device. Software clones minted overnight lack the lantern of hardware proof, so they enter the garden of peer trust as powerless strangers: spinning up ten thousand fakes buys zero weight, because no peer grants influence to an unauthenticated voice. The defense scales because hardware identity is expensive to counterfeit but cheap to verify.
